thread.title: Intel (INTC) 2nd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Intel (INTC) 2nd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Intel ( INTC ) is set to report second quarter fiscal 2018 earnings results after the closing bell Thursday. And the semiconductor giant can use a strong top- and bottom-line beat to get the bears off its back.
Intel’s shares have been rocky ever since the abrupt resignation of CEO Brian Krzanich on June 21. Upon which the Intel’s board of directors stated it was searching for a new CEO internally and externally. Prior to his departure, however, Krzanich told analysts that Intel was on the verge of losing some server processor market share to Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ). There are also rumors that Intel could have a major victory by being the sole provider of wireless chips in Apple’s ( AAPL ) next iPhone.
In its post-earnings conference call with analysts Wednesday rival Qualcomm ( QCOM ) was overly candid, saying Apple would rely solely on a competitor's modem chips in its next iPhone. While Qualcomm didn’t refer to Intel by name, it’s known that Intel and Qualcomm were the only two splitting the modem components within the iPhones. And with Intel having added CDMA connections in its wireless chips, it only makes sense that almost Intel would be the unnamed competitor Qualcomm referred to.
In other words, investors are likely to get tons of answers to several important topics on Thursday. Or new ones will be asked. Interim CEO Bob Swan, is also expected to provide details on the progress on the search for the company’s new leader.
For the quarter that ended June, the Santa Clara, Calif.-based company is expected to earn 96 cents per share on revenue of $16.76 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 72 cents per share on revenue of $14.76 billion. For the full year, EPS is expected to rise 15.89% year over year to $4.01 per share, while full-year revenue of $68.43 billion would rise 9% year over year.
Given that the company has posted ten straight earnings beats, Intel has been one of the better-executing companies on the Dow, despite its recent pullback. While revenue in its client-computing segment (traditional PC,) is expect to grow just 3.3% to $8.48 billion from the year-ago period, Intel more than makes up for that in its Data-center group, or DGC, business, which is expected to surge 28% to $5.61 billion.
Elsewhere, the Nonvolatile memory solutions segment is expected to see some 26% year-over-year revenue growth to $1.1 billion, while the “Internet of Things,” or IoT, revenue is expected to grow 18% to $853 million. Investors should also expect an update on the company’s full-year forecast. But Ross Seymore, analyst at Deutsche Bank who has a Buy and a $64 price target on Intel, expects a downbeat forecast from the company after its stellar first-half performance in data-center and client-computing segments.
